entry.title: Add the published HuggingFace and ModelScope model links to the README
entry.content:
Add the published HuggingFace and ModelScope model links to the README

RynnLAM and the Stage-1 RynnVLA-Latent-2B/4B checkpoints are now published
on both hubs, so document them in a new "Model weights" section, point the
RynnLAM Optional-components bullet at it, and narrow the TODO(hf) to the
still-unpublished RynnBrain backbones and DA3-Large encoder. The code repo
still ships no weights; the 2B/4B exports are Stage-1 initializations, not
closed-loop policies.

entry.title: Correct comments that the remediation edits left inaccurate
entry.content:
Correct comments that the remediation edits left inaccurate

Comment-only, plus one dead branch. No behaviour change beyond the removed fallback.

- write_npz claimed the skip check "trusts existence". It has not since npz_is_complete
  landed beside it; the atomic publish is now justified by what it actually buys -- no
  reader, including a rebuild_latent_manifest sweep running concurrently with labeling,
  can observe a partial file at the final path.
- npz_is_complete accepted a bare "latent_action" member as well as the ".npy" form.
  np.savez appends ".npy" to every key unconditionally, so that branch could never be
  taken, and keeping it blurred the very trap the docstring exists to record.
- The largest-remainder comment pointed at "the inner one at line ~730", a line number
  the surrounding edits had already moved.
- Reflowed four comment blocks whose right edge the corpus-scale scrub left ragged.

entry.title: Add HuggingFace model-card metadata to the README
entry.content:
Add HuggingFace model-card metadata to the README

The README is uploaded verbatim as the model card, so without front-matter the hub
shows no license badge, no pipeline tag and nothing to discover the repo by.

base_model is left commented out rather than filled in: the hub warns about and drops
an id that does not resolve to a live repo, and the RynnBrain-2B/4B backbones are not
published yet. This distribution ships no weights, so nothing here is a fine-tune of
anything -- declaring a base would be a claim the repo cannot back.

entry.title: Add the complete RynnVLA-Latent source release
entry.content:
Add the complete RynnVLA-Latent source release

Assembles the open-source release from the three internal repositories so a
fresh clone can run the whole chain offline: RynnLAM training, latent-action
labeling, Stage-1 latent-action VLA pretraining, Stage-2 post-training, and
evaluation.

Baseline is the previously curated RynnVLA-LA draft, reconciled file by file
against the internal codebase. Beyond that draft this adds:

- Stage-2 knobs: transfer_lr / transfer_modules (an independent peak LR for
  inherited modules) and sampler_shuffle (episode-locality vs global order).
  Both are resume-critical, so constants.RESUME_CRITICAL_FIELDS gained the
  matching keys.
- scripts/build_dataset_weights.py: temperature (alpha) reweighting of a
  Stage-1 latent mixture. The per-dataset targets are a largest-remainder
  rounding that sums back to the natural total, so len(dataset) -- and the
  max_steps derived from it -- does not move when an arm is reweighted.
- The RoboTwin and VLABench tracks: both datasets, the shared video-decode
  helpers, the two Stage-2 recipes, example mixtures, the VLABench policy
  server and the RoboTwin policy adapter, plus
  scripts/build_robotwin_index.py to produce the episode index RoboTwinDataset
  requires and nothing previously shipped could build.
- tests/: 27 CPU-only test files, 392 passing. They run offline in under a
  minute and are the fastest way to confirm an install actually works.

Three defects found while reconciling are fixed rather than carried over: the
resume path only applied node-local staging for resume=True and not for the
resolved-checkpoint string, so api.train callers missed it; q01_q99 action
normalization offset by q01 instead of the midpoint, which does not suit a
flow head sampling N(0, 1); and the alpha-weighted virtual index was laid out
dataset-major, which the locality sampler cannot tile, so it silently degraded
to a plain randperm and cost 5.2x wall clock at alpha=0.7.

The simulator side of RoboTwin and VLABench is deliberately not bundled, so
no command here reproduces a benchmark score; README states that next to the
claim it qualifies, and lists what to bring. NOTICE now records the policy
server's listening socket and its pickle framing, which the previous "no
network access at runtime" wording contradicted.
